scientific_question: Does increasing SINR consistently correspond to decreasing link-error probability across the revision-time source reconstruction, the independent coded Sionna link, and public real O-RAN measurements?

claim_scope.supported_claim: The 48-bit uncoded PER quantity is a trend-level reliability proxy whose expected SINR-to-error direction can be compared with coded BLER and measured DL-BLER.
prohibited_claims: The 48-bit PER proxy is numerically calibrated to post-LDPC BLER.
The 48-bit proxy reproduces HARQ failure probability.
Error-rate magnitudes are directly comparable across the three systems.
A significant association establishes causal equivalence between systems.

common_preprocessing.missing_values: Use listwise deletion only for the variables required by the current endpoint. No imputation.

mcs_canonicalization.source_and_sionna: MCS must be finite and within 1e-6 of an integer. Canonicalize using nearest-integer rounding.
mcs_canonicalization.zenodo: Treat phy_mcs as a continuous or aggregated telemetry variable. Do not round, discretize, bin, or threshold it.

common_preprocessing.ties: Use average ranks for tied values.

mcs_stratified_rank_correlation.name: MCS-stratified Spearman correlation
algorithm: Within each independent sequence or recording file, divide observations by the canonical integer MCS value.
Discard an MCS stratum only when it has fewer than the preregistered minimum number of finite observations or when SINR or the error variable is constant.
Within each retained MCS stratum, replace SINR and the error variable by average ranks.
Center and standardize both rank variables within that MCS stratum.
Concatenate the standardized within-stratum ranks and compute their Pearson correlation.
mcs_stratified_rank_correlation.interpretation: This estimates a monotonic SINR-error association after removing between-MCS level differences.

source_analysis.support_rule: The median correlation is negative and the upper bound of its 95% bootstrap interval is below zero.
secondary_descriptive_endpoints: Sequence-level Spearman correlation between BER and PER_proxy; expected positive.
Absolute deviation between observed PER_proxy and 1-(1-BER)^48; descriptive only because bit errors need not be independent.

sionna_analysis.support_rule: The median correlation is negative and the upper bound of its 95% bootstrap interval is below zero.
sionna_analysis.secondary_descriptive_endpoint: Sequence-level Spearman correlation between pre-LDPC BER and post-LDPC BLER; expected positive.

bler_unit_normalization.ratio_rule: When every finite BLER value is within [0,1+1e-8], retain it as a ratio.
bler_unit_normalization.percentage_rule: Otherwise, when every finite value is within [0,100+1e-8] and at least one value exceeds 1+1e-8, divide all BLER values by 100.
bler_unit_normalization.invalid_rule: Any other range fails the analysis.
bler_unit_normalization.post_normalization: Clip only numerical tolerance violations within 1e-8 to [0,1].

zenodo_analysis.primary_file_effect: Partial Spearman correlation between dl_sinr and dl_bler while controlling continuous phy_mcs.
partial_spearman_algorithm: Within each recording file, retain rows with finite dl_sinr, normalized dl_bler, and phy_mcs.
Replace dl_sinr, normalized dl_bler, and phy_mcs by average ranks.
Regress the dl_sinr ranks on an intercept and the phy_mcs ranks using ordinary least squares.
Regress the dl_bler ranks on the same intercept and phy_mcs ranks.
Compute Pearson correlation between the two residual vectors.

primary_aggregate.transform: Apply Fisher arctanh to each eligible file-level correlation.
primary_aggregate.aggregate: Arithmetic mean in Fisher-z space, transformed back using tanh.

exact_direction_test.method: Enumerate all 2^10 sign-flip patterns over the ten independent file-level Fisher-z effects.

zenodo_analysis.support_rule: All ten files must be eligible; the equal-weight Fisher-z aggregate partial Spearman correlation must be negative; the exact one-sided file sign-flip p-value must be below 0.05; and the upper bound of the file-cluster bootstrap interval must be below zero.
mandatory_reporting: excluded file count and fixed reason
partial Spearman effect for every file
number of files with negative effects
BLER unit decision for every file

secondary_multiplicity.role: Exploratory only; no secondary endpoint may replace the primary endpoint.

cross_system_interpretation.full_directional_support: Source, Sionna, and Zenodo all satisfy their preregistered support rules.
cross_system_interpretation.coded_and_real_support: Sionna and Zenodo satisfy their support rules, supporting transfer of the reliability direction beyond the uncoded source proxy.
cross_system_interpretation.partial_support: At least one but not all systems satisfy their support rules.
cross_system_interpretation.no_support: None of the three systems satisfies its support rule.

prohibited_posthoc_actions: Replace dl_bler as the Zenodo primary outcome
Choose a temporal lag after observing results
Smooth BLER or SINR after observing results
Remove recording files because their effects are unfavorable
Promote a secondary endpoint to primary
Select a diagnostic threshold using these reliability analyses
Claim equality between PER_proxy and coded BLER magnitudes
Round Zenodo phy_mcs to an integer after observing its encoding.
Bin or discretize Zenodo phy_mcs after observing results.
Replace continuous-MCS partial Spearman with the invalid V1 integer-stratified estimator.

supersedes.reason: The V1 protocol incorrectly assumed that Zenodo phy_mcs was a discrete integer index. A metadata-only encoding audit showed that 57584 of 59798 finite values were noninteger. No SINR-BLER association was inspected when making this amendment.
